title: Adaptive retention bands and sprint-upgrade offering for isolated on-prem customers
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Experiment to validate a modular license + ops-credit model for Private/VPC and on-prem customers that need predictable upgrades and emergency response.

Hypothesis: bundling a base license fee with configurable 'retention bands' (0/30/90-day upgrade windows) plus an optional monthly 'sprint-upgrade' add-on and an 'entropy insurance' retainer for emergency patches will increase contract ARR and reduce unplanned engineering load for high-touch customers.

Scope: define three retention bands (Standard: 90-day functional cadence + monthly security backport; Accelerated: 30-day functional cadence; Locked: 0-day scheduled upgrades only with paid sprint option), pricing for sprint-upgrade SKU, ops-credit ladder for incident response windows, and contract language to support rollback windows and downgrade grace. Pilot with 3 enterprise customers with differing upgrade risk profiles to collect WTP, SLA acceptance, and operational impact metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Price points defined for Base License + 3 retention bands and Sprint SKU (target 3 pricing anchors)
Legal-approved contract amendments ready (change log + sample clause) and Security Questionnaire answers updated
Billing SKUs created and verified in test tenant; usage example flows documented
Pilot customers (>=3) signed LOI to trial offering for >=90 days
Operational runbook for sprint upgrades and entropy insurance invoked at least once during pilot
Success metrics instrumented: upgrade completion rate, mean time to rollback (MTTRollback), ops-hours per incident, incremental ARR from add-ons
